title: Monomers and Polymers
short: Large biological molecules are chains of small units. Dehydration synthesis joins monomers and releases water; hydrolysis splits polymers by adding water.
trouble: Students reverse the two reactions, thinking water is added to build a chain. Building a bond removes a water molecule; breaking one uses a water molecule.

blocks.html: Cells build huge molecules (starch, proteins, DNA) the way you build a train: link small cars, one at a time. The small units are monomers ("one part"); the chains are polymers ("many parts"). The same two reactions build and break all of them.
Dehydration synthesis joins two monomers and releases a water molecule. Hydrolysis splits a polymer by adding a water molecule to each bond.

blocks.name: bi-molecule
blocks.cap: Join the monomers and watch a water molecule leave at each new bond; split them and water goes back in.

blocks.html: To link two monomers, the cell takes an –OH from one and an –H from the other. Those leave together as H₂O ("dehydration": water removed), and the two monomers share a new covalent bond. Hydrolysis ("water splitting") runs it backward: a water molecule is split, its –H and –OH go back on, and the bond breaks. Digestion is hydrolysis: enzymes in your gut add water to break starch and proteins into sugars and amino acids.

blocks.title: Count the water
blocks.q: A cell joins 5 glucose molecules into a short chain. How many water molecules are released?
steps: Each new bond between two neighbors releases one water.
A chain of 5 has 4 bonds between neighbors (like 5 train cars have 4 couplings).

blocks.title: Follow the atoms
blocks.q: Glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆. What is the formula of the disaccharide made by joining two glucose molecules?

items: Nucleic acids: monomers are nucleotides (Nucleic Acids).
Lipids are the exception: they are not long chains of one repeating monomer (Lipids).

blocks.html: Reversing the two reactions, thinking water is added to build a chain. Read the names: dehydration means water is taken out, and it happens when a bond is made; hydro-lysis means water splits something, and it happens when a bond is broken. Quick check: counting atoms, the chain is lighter than its monomers added up, by one water per bond.
